root.claim: One deterministic Turing machine with a fixed finite alphabet and a fixed number of one-dimensional tapes outputs $\operatorname{bin}_{2n}(\operatorname{val}(x)\operatorname{val}(y))$ for every $n\ge1$ and all $n$-bit inputs $x,y$, in worst-case time $O(n(\lg n)^{1-\kappa})$ with $\kappa=2^{-182}$.
root.method: Reduce multiplication to a cyclic convolution evaluated by Fourier transforms on power-of-two axes, accelerate the transforms' address rearrangements and butterfly layers by two tape procedures built from fixed linear networks with a rank saving, and bound every cost divided by the volume $V=Tp=\Theta(n)$.

motivation.text: A transform-based multiplier that scans its $\Theta(n)$-bit array once per level of a $\Theta(\log n)$-level transform already costs $\Theta(n\log n)$; beating the conjecture requires making both the data movement and the butterfly arithmetic of the levels cheaper than full scans.

quote.quote:
Scanning an array of $\Theta(n)$ stored bits at each of
$\Theta(\log n)$ transform levels already costs $\Theta(n\log n)$.
We therefore need savings in both movement and arithmetic.

children.claim: To refute the eventual $\Omega(n\lg n)$ lower bound in the fixed-tape model it suffices to give one machine with $\liminf_{n\to\infty}T_A(n)/(n\lg n)=0$, and a bound $O(n(\lg n)^{1-\kappa})$ gives limit zero through all input lengths.

quote.quote:
Its negation requires one machine satisfying
$\liminf_{n\to\infty}T_A(n)/(n\lg n)=0$.

children.claim: Two disjoint contiguous address chunks of $u$ bits in an arbitrary bit array on $[P]\times[2^u]\times[G]\times[2^u]\times[B]$ can be interchanged, $(p,h,g,d,z)\mapsto(p,d,g,h,z)$, in $O(Vu^\tau)$ steps with a fixed $\tau<1$, where $V=PGB\,2^{2u}$.
children.method: Prove the bound for chunks of $e=m^k$ radix-$q$ digits with a row field divisible by $W^k$ through the bit network, then manufacture that row field from a few high digits, split the remaining width in base $m$, and pad binary chunks to radix $q$.

motivation.text: The network recursion needs a row field long enough to be split $k$ times into $W$ role streams; borrowing $O(\log e)$ high digits of the chunks supplies it at a cost below the target bound.

quote.quote:
Rows for a general array can be supplied by a few of its own high digits.
Their movement will cost less than the final bound.

children.claim: For $e=m^k$, two disjoint chunks of $e$ radix-$q$ digits preceded by a row field whose length is divisible by $W^k$ can be interchanged in $O(Ve^\tau)$ time, because the time per volume obeys $F_k\le(s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1)$ with $s/W<m^\tau$.
children.method: Deal whole rows cyclically to $W$ role streams, run the fixed bit network on them pointwise with address-shear frames whose endpoint differences are the identity, implement each edge's change of frame by as many smaller interchanges as the rank of its matrix, and solve the resulting recurrence.

motivation.text: Dividing cost by volume, one level of recursion multiplies the parameter by $m$ but the recursive contribution only by $s/W$; the strict inequality $s<Wm$ is exactly what turns the trivial cost linear in $e$ into $e^\tau$ with $\tau<1$.

quote.quote:
Because the sum of these ranks is less than the number of wires times
$m$, the resulting recurrence saves a power of the chunk width.

children.claim: The fixed scalar network on banks $X_a,Y_a$ (indexed by triples $a$ of three-element subsets of $[100]$), whose three stages run forward, inverse and forward eight-row invocations, sends $(X_a,Y_a)\mapsto(-Y_a,X_a)$, which over $\mathbb F_2$ is the exchange of the two banks, and restores every scratch wire whatever its initial value.
children.method: Show that one eight-row invocation adds $x$ to $y$ independently of the scratch values by computing its net copy, gather, scatter and side-injection coefficients, then compose the three stages.

motivation.text: Subtracting the effect of the old scratch values first and restoring them last makes the net map independent of the scratch contents, so arbitrary rows of the array can later serve as scratch wires.

quote.quote:
The first two rows of
the following schedule remove the effect of the old scratch values;
the next four introduce the source values and add their effect to the
target; the last two restore the scratch values.

children.claim: With initial side and central vectors $a,c$, rows 0–1 subtract $\mathcal Ja+\mathcal Rc$, rows 2–3 change the scratch to $a+\mathcal Vx$, $c+\mathcal Gx$, rows 4–5 add $\mathcal R(c+\mathcal Gx)+\mathcal J(a+\mathcal Vx)$ and rows 6–7 restore $a,c$, so the net effect is $y\gets y+(\mathcal J\mathcal V+\mathcal R\mathcal G)x$ for every $a,c$.

quote.quote:
The net target change is
$(\mathcal J\mathcal V+\mathcal R\mathcal G)x$, independently of
$a,c$.

children.claim: In the bit case the gather–scatter coefficient from $x_T$ to $y_S$ is $|S\cap T|\bmod 2$; side wires join exactly the pairs with $|S\cap T|=1$ and cancel them, pairs with intersection $0$ or $2$ already have coefficient $0$, and $S=T$ gives $1$, so $\mathcal J\mathcal V+\mathcal R\mathcal G=I$ and the invocation performs $y\gets y+x$.

quote.quote:
In the bit case, the central coefficient from $x_T$ to $y_S$ is
$|S\cap T|\bmod2$.  The side contribution cancels exactly the
intersection-one cases

children.claim: Running stage 1 forward ($Y\gets Y+X$), stage 2 inverse ($X\gets X-Y$) and stage 3 forward gives $(x,y)\mapsto(x,y+x)\mapsto(-y,y+x)\mapsto(-y,x)$, and each invocation restores its own scratch wires.

quote.quote:
Starting from $(x,y)$, the three stages give
$(x,y+x)$, then $(-y,y+x)$, then $(-y,x)$.

children.salient: The exchange is exact for every initial content of the scratch wires, so scratch roles never need to be cleared.

children.claim: If each scalar is replaced by an array on a common address set $\Omega$, each source, gate and sink $v$ is given an invertible linear frame $D_v$, and $D_vD_u^{-1}$ is applied on each edge from $u$ to $v$, then the network implements $D_{\rm out}\mathsf S_\Omega D_{\rm in}^{-1}$, so a route from role $w$ to role $\rho(w)$ with scalar sign $\varepsilon_w$ applies $\varepsilon_wD_{\mathrm{sink}(\rho(w))}D_{\mathrm{source}(w)}^{-1}$.
children.method: Maintain along edges and through pointwise gates the invariant that the stored array at each vertex is its frame applied to the logical array.

motivation.text: Separating the endpoint operator, which only the terminal frames determine, from the intermediate frames leaves the latter free to be chosen so that every edge change is cheap.

quote.quote:
Once the scalar routing is fixed,
the endpoint frames determine the array operator on each route; the
intermediate frames can then be chosen to make each edge change inexpensive.

children.claim: All incidences of a gate share the frame $D_v$, and linearity gives $\sum_jc_jD_v\varphi_j=D_v(\sum_jc_j\varphi_j)$, so the common frame commutes with the pointwise gate and the invariant passes from the sources to the sinks.

quote.quote:
Thus the common frame commutes with the pointwise gate, and
the invariant continues to the sinks.

children.claim: Hence the implemented operator is $D_{\rm out}\mathsf S_\Omega D_{\rm in}^{-1}$, and for a signed role permutation each route, auxiliary routes included, applies $\varepsilon_wD_{\mathrm{sink}(\rho(w))}D_{\mathrm{source}(w)}^{-1}$.

quote.quote:
All roles, including
the auxiliary roles, enter this identity.

children.salient: The intermediate frames cancel completely: only the two endpoint frames of a route affect what it does.

children.claim: Giving each gate and sink the projection $M_v=P_U$ onto its label $U$, a nondegenerate subspace of $\mathcal F=(\mathbb Q^{h})^{\otimes3}$ of dimension $m=h^3$ built from triple indicators, and giving $X_a$ the source matrix $-P_{U_a}$, makes every endpoint difference $M_{\mathrm{sink}(\rho(w))}-M_{\mathrm{source}(w)}$ equal to $I_m$ while the ranks of all edge differences sum to $s_{\rm b}=W_{\rm b}m-N+2L_{\rm b}<W_{\rm b}m$.
children.method: Use the bilinear form $x^{\mathsf T}(I-J/9)y$, under which neighboring triple indicators are orthogonal, to prescribe nested labels stage by stage, count dimension changes edge by edge (they telescope at gates), and add the extra rank of the negative source projections.

motivation.text: The signed dimension changes are fixed by the terminal labels at $Wm-2N$ and ranks equal absolute changes, so the only freedom is the total loss on decreasing edges, which must stay below $N/2$ for the rank sum to fall below $Wm$.

quote.quote:
The saving will come from keeping the total dimension lost on decreasing
edges small relative to $N$.

children.claim: Under $\langle x,y\rangle=x^{\mathsf T}(I-J/9)y$ on $\mathbb Q^{h}$ (eigenvalues $1$ and $-91/9$, so nondegenerate), triple indicators satisfy $\langle t_S,t_T\rangle=|S\cap T|-1$ and $\langle t_T,t_T\rangle=2$, so every triple line is nondegenerate and neighboring triples ($|S\cap T|=1$) are orthogonal.

quote.quote:
Thus every triple line is nondegenerate, and neighboring triple lines
are orthogonal, in the label field belonging to either construction.

children.claim: On a side wire joining neighboring triples with indicators $t_X,t_Y$, the remaining label component can pass through $P\otimes\langle t_X\rangle\subset P\otimes t_Y^\perp\subset P\otimes F$, which is possible only because $t_X\perp t_Y$.

quote.quote: The first inclusion is possible because $t_X\perp t_Y$.

children.claim: Every edge joins comparable nondegenerate labels and label dimension never decreases along an edge, with one exception: the central-wire edge from time 3 to time 4, which loses $P\otimes F\otimes Q$ of dimension $h$; with $I$ invocations and $c$ central wires each, the total loss is $L=Ich$.

quote.quote:
The only decreasing
edges are the central-wire edges from time 3 to time 4; their dimension
loss is $h$.

children.claim: Each touched wire has one incoming and one outgoing incidence at a gate with the same label, so the signed dimension changes telescope to the sink total $Wm-N$ minus the source total $N$, i.e. $Wm-2N$, and the absolute changes sum to $Wm-2N+2L$.

quote.quote:
The signed sum of dimension changes telescopes at every gate: each
touched wire has one incoming and one outgoing incidence with the same
gate label.

children.claim: The loss ratio is $L_{\rm b}/N=100/539$, smaller than $1/2$.

quote.quote: In particular, both are smaller than $1/2$.

children.claim: For nested nondegenerate $U\subset V$, $P_V-P_U$ is the projection onto $V\cap U^\perp$, so its rank is $\dim V-\dim U$; the only exceptions are the $N$ first edges on the $X_a$, whose matrix $P_{U_a}-(-P_{U_a})=2P_{U_a}$ has rank one where the dimension change is zero, so $s_{\rm b}=(W_{\rm b}m-2N+2L_{\rm b})+N=W_{\rm b}m-N+2L_{\rm b}$, short of $W_{\rm b}m$ by $N-2L_{\rm b}>0$.

quote.quote: The only exceptions are the $N$ negative source projections.

children.claim: For an input $X_a$ the endpoint difference is $P_{U_a^\perp}-(-P_{U_a})=I_m$, and every other role has zero source matrix and identity sink matrix, so every route differs by exactly $I_m$.

quote.quote:
For an input $X_a$ the endpoint difference is
$P_{U_a^\perp}-(-P_{U_a})=I_m$.

children.salient: The total rank of all edge changes is strictly below the trivial count $Wm$, and the gap comes only from intersection sizes of three-element subsets through $\langle t_S,t_T\rangle=|S\cap T|-1$.

adds.name: bank pair count
adds.meaning: The number $\binom{100}{3}^3$ of index triples $a$, that is, of data pairs $(X_a,Y_a)$ the network exchanges.

adds.name: lost dimension
adds.meaning: The total label dimension lost on the decreasing edges of the network.

adds.name: ground set size
adds.meaning: The number $100$ of points whose three-element subsets index the data.

children.claim: The relative deficit $(W_{\rm b}m-s_{\rm b})/(W_{\rm b}m)=339/22587335000000$ exceeds $20\cdot2^{-50}$, and $\log m<20$ gives $m^{1-2^{-50}}>m(1-20\cdot2^{-50})$, so $s/W<m^\tau$ with $\tau=1-2^{-50}$.

quote.quote: Both exact deficits displayed above are greater than $20\cdot2^{-50}$.

children.claim: For a rational $m\times m$ matrix $A$ of rank $a$, the address permutation $(H,D)\mapsto(H+AD,D)$ on two groups of $m$ fields over $\mathbb Z/q^b$ (with $q$ a fixed prime avoiding all denominators) costs exactly $a$ interchanges of pairs of $b$-digit fields plus $O(V)$ further work, and the three shears $D\gets D-H$, $H\gets H+D$, $D\gets H-D$ interchange $H$ and $D$.
children.method: Factor $A=E_1\Pi E_2$ with invertible lower-triangular $E_1,E_2$ and a partial permutation $\Pi$ with $a$ ones, apply the triangular factors as controlled shifts in linear time, and realize each one of $\Pi$ by a single field interchange between two controlled shifts.

motivation.text: Controlled shifts update a later field from earlier fields in linear time, so lower-triangular coordinate changes are cheap and only the rank-many entries of $\Pi$ call for genuine interchanges.

quote.quote:
Lemma~\ref{lem:ordered-affine-streams} updates a later field using
earlier fields in linear time.  Lower triangular changes of coordinates
can be performed entirely in this direction.

children.claim: Every rational $m\times m$ matrix of rank $a$ factors as $E_1\Pi E_2$ with invertible lower-triangular $E_1,E_2$ and $\Pi$ having exactly $a$ ones, at most one per row and column (a Bruhat factorization with the coordinate order reversed, found by eliminating with the rightmost entry of the topmost nonzero row as pivot).

quote.quote:
where $E_1,E_2$ are invertible lower triangular rational matrices and
$\Pi$ has exactly $a$ entries equal to one

children.claim: A lower-triangular transformation of $H$ or of $D$ costs $O(V)$: coordinates are updated in descending physical order, each by a controlled shift from earlier coordinates that still hold their original values.

quote.quote:
A lower triangular transformation of $H$, or of $D$, costs $O(V)$:
update coordinates in descending physical order.

children.claim: A one of $\Pi$ at $(i,j)$, i.e. $H_i\gets H_i+D_j$, is done by $D_j\gets D_j+H_i$, $(H_i,D_j)\gets(D_j,H_i)$, $D_j\gets H_i-D_j$, which takes $(h,d)$ to $(h+d,d)$ with one interchange, so the number of recursive calls is exactly the rank $a$.

quote.quote:
On an initial pair $(h,d)$ this sequence yields $(h+d,d)$.
It uses just one interchange.

children.claim: The updates $D\gets D-H$, $H\gets H+D$, $D\gets H-D$ send $(H,D)$ to $(D,H)$; only the middle shear needs the network, while the outer two target the later group and cost $O(V)$.

quote.quote:
The other two
updates target the later group and have linear cost.

children.claim: Within each prefix, row $Wg+(w-1)$ goes to role stream $w$ as row $g$, so the $W$ streams have the same address shape, including the full ranges of $H$ and $D$, each with logical volume $V/W$ and a row count divisible by $W^{k-1}$; this supplies the common address set of the frame identity.

quote.quote:
These streams have exactly the same remaining shape, including the
full ranges of $H$ and $D$.

children.claim: With the frame $\Phi_{M_v}$ moving $(H,D)$ to $(H+M_vD,D)$, which commutes with pointwise XOR gates, the output on role $\rho(w)$ is $\Phi_{M_{\mathrm{out}(\rho(w))}}\Phi_{-M_{\mathrm{in}(w)}}f_w=\Phi_{I_m}f_w$, so after the rows are merged back every original row, scratch rows included, has undergone $H\gets H+D$.

quote.quote:
The result
is $H\leftarrow H+D$ on every original row, including rows assigned
to scratch roles, whose initial values were arbitrary.

children.claim: An edge whose matrix has rank $a$ costs $a$ recursive interchanges of $(e/m)$-digit fields on one stream of volume $V/W$, so one invocation makes exactly $s$ smaller calls, while splitting, merging, gates and triangular updates are fixed in number and cost $O(V)$; hence $F_0=O(1)$ and $F_k\le(s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1)$.

quote.quote: The number of recursive calls is the sum of the edge ranks, exactly $s$.

children.claim: With $s/W<m^\tau$ the unrolled sum $\sum_{j\le k}(s/W)^j$ is $O(m^{k\tau})$ (at most $k+1$ if $s/W\le1$), so $F_k=O(e^\tau)$.

quote.quote: Hence $F_k=O(e^\tau)$.

children.claim: Parking the $W-1$ inactive role streams on a stack around each child call and restoring them costs $O(V)$ at a node with only $s$ children, so the fixed-tape schedule adds nothing to the factor $s/W$.

quote.quote:
Temporary storage is
therefore not substituted for logical volume in the factor $s/W$.

children.salient: The exponent $\tau<1$ is strict although the deficit is minute: $s_{\rm b}/(W_{\rm b}m)$ falls short of one only by $339/22587335000000$, yet any strict deficit compounds over the $\log_m e$ recursion levels into a power saving in $e$.

adds.name: wire count
adds.meaning: The number of wires of the fixed bit network, scratch wires included; rows of the array are dealt cyclically to these roles.

adds.name: label dimension
adds.meaning: The dimension $100^3$ of the label space, which is also the number of digit fields each chunk is cut into at one recursion level.

adds.name: smaller call count
adds.meaning: The sum of the ranks of all edge matrices, that is, the number of smaller interchanges one run of the network makes.

adds.name: normalized cost
adds.meaning: An upper bound on time divided by logical volume for interchanging two chunks of $m^k$ digits.

children.claim: For $e$-digit chunks with $k=\lceil\log_me\rceil$, exchanging and joining the top $\rho=O(\log e)$ digits of both chunks creates a row field of range $q^{2\rho}\ge W^k$ in front of the remaining chunks at cost $O(V\rho)$, and zero rows pad its count to a multiple of $W^k$ at most doubling the volume.

quote.quote: In the two middle orders, the first two fields form a row field of range

children.claim: Writing $e-\rho=\sum_ja_jm^j$ with $0\le a_j<m$ and interchanging corresponding pieces of width $m^j$ costs $O(V)\sum_ja_jm^{j\tau}=O(Ve^\tau)$, a geometric sum because $a_j<m$ and $m^k<me$.

quote.quote:
The fixed bound $a_j<m$ and the inequality $m^k<me$ make this a
geometric sum of the stated order.

children.claim: Binary chunks of $u$ bits are padded numerically to $[q^e]$ with $e=O(u)$, which enlarges the volume by a fixed factor, so the interchange costs $O(Vu^\tau)$.

quote.quote:
Since $e=O(u)$ for fixed $q$, the bound is
$O(Vu^\tau)$.

children.salient: The result is an exact permutation of the data, yet it is computed through XOR combinations of intermediate data and costs fewer scans than moving the $u$ address bits one at a time.

children.claim: On an array $[P]\times[2^K]^D\times[S]$ with $D\le d$ whose records are polynomials with $r$ complex disk-grid coefficients, applying $H_0(u,v)=((u+v)/2,(u-v)/2)$ to the bit at a common offset of each of the $D$ chunks and truncating once returns $Q_p(\mathcal Hz)$, with error less than $\sqrt2\,2^{-p}$, in $O(Vd^{\lambda'})$ time for a fixed $\lambda'<1$.
children.method: Write $H_0^{\otimes D}=b^D\mathcal S_DC^{\otimes D}\mathcal S_D$, compute $C^{\otimes e}$ recursively with the complex phase network on row streams whose binary changes of basis are packed selected-bit additions, unroll the recurrence, and reserve guard bits so that the whole layer is exact before one truncation.

motivation.text: Applying the $D$ butterflies axis by axis costs $D$ full passes, which over all transform rounds would restore the $n\log n$ cost; a simultaneous layer in $O(Vd^{\lambda'})$ saves a power of $d$.

quote.quote:
We will obtain cost $O(Vd^{\lambda'})$, with
$\lambda'<1$ and $V$ the logical bit volume, whereas separate butterfly
factors would require $D$ whole-array passes.

children.claim: With phase frames $\mathcal C_U=H^{\otimes m}\operatorname{diag}(i^{\operatorname{wt}(P_Ux)\bmod 4})H^{\otimes m}$ on the binary labels, each edge's frame change is a product of one kernel $aI+bX_v$ or its inverse per vector $v$ of an orthonormal basis of the edge residual; hence on $e=mf$ selected axes the complex network yields $C^{\otimes e}$ on every role from $s_{\rm c}<W_{\rm c}m$ forward child calls on $f$ axes, and $H_0^{\otimes D}=b^D\mathcal S_DC^{\otimes D}\mathcal S_D$.
children.method: Use additivity of Hamming weight modulo four on orthogonal vectors to factor frame changes into translation kernels, move those directions to coordinate slots with a binary change of basis $\mathcal P_M$, and fix endpoint signs with $C=iZC^{-1}Z$.

motivation.text: The two-point kernel plays the role the address shear plays for bits: frame changes become products of $C$ on fewer selected axes, so the same rank-saving recursion applies to butterflies.

quote.quote:
Its phase
frames express a $C$ tensor product using smaller groups of
selected bits, separated by binary changes of basis.

children.claim: For binary $z,w$ with $z\cdot w=0$ the supports meet in an even number of points, so $\operatorname{wt}(z+w)\equiv\operatorname{wt}(z)+\operatorname{wt}(w)\pmod4$; for $V=U\perp E$ this gives $q_V-q_U=\sum_{v}\operatorname{wt}(v)[v\cdot x]$ over an orthonormal basis of $E$, and each odd-weight $v$ contributes the kernel $aI+bX_v$ or its inverse.

quote.quote:
If $z\cdot w=0$, the intersection cardinality is even, so weight is
additive modulo four.

children.claim: The number of residual basis vectors over the whole complex network is $s_{\rm c}=W_{\rm c}m-2N+2L_{\rm c}$, short of $W_{\rm c}m$ by $2N-2L_{\rm c}>0$ since $L_{\rm c}/N=101/539<1/2$.

quote.quote: The deficit is $2N-2L_{\rm c}>0$.

children.claim: Conjugating by the address permutation $\mathcal P_M$ whose first columns are the residual basis turns the edge change into coordinate kernels, and $(C^{-1})^{\otimes f}=(-i)^fZ^{\otimes f}C^{\otimes f}Z^{\otimes f}$, so each basis vector costs exactly one forward child $C^{\otimes f}$ on the $f$ axes of one slot.

quote.quote:
A negative directional kernel still requires only one
forward child, because

children.claim: $\mathcal P_M$ is a product of at most $m(m-1)+3m$ elementary row additions over $\mathbb F_2$, each of which XORs corresponding selected bits of two whole slots.

quote.quote:
Thus one row addition changes corresponding selected
positions in two whole slots.

children.claim: Summing residual dimensions gives exactly $s_{\rm c}$ child calls on $f=e/m$ axes, and the endpoint $Z$ signs, the scalar $i^{27f}$ and negation of the physical $X$ outputs make every role, scratch roles included, receive $C^{\otimes e}$.

quote.quote:
Summing its residual dimensions gives exactly
$s_{\rm c}$ child calls, each on the $f=e/m$ axes of one slot.

children.claim: Since $H_0=b\mathsf SC\mathsf S$, $H_0^{\otimes D}=b^D\mathcal S_DC^{\otimes D}\mathcal S_D$ with $b^D=(-i/2)^{\lfloor D/2\rfloor}b^{D\bmod 2}$, so converting to normalized butterflies costs only a binary shift and fourth-root phases.

quote.quote:
so it is a binary shift and fourth-root phase, with at most one further
factor $b$.

adds.name: two-point kernel
adds.meaning: The $2\times2$ matrix $aI+bX$ with $a=(1+i)/2$ and $b=(1-i)/2$, from which the butterfly layer is assembled.

children.claim: On a rectangle with three $L=fK$-bit address chunks $x,y,z$ and $R$-bit records, the XORs $y_{j_i}\gets y_{j_i}\oplus x_{j_i}$ at the $f$ positions $j_i=\rho+iK$ can be done together, restoring $z$ for every initial value, in $O(V(L^\tau+1)+MA_{\rm rect}^3+\delta_{\rm bad}MA_{\rm rect}(R+A_{\rm rect}))$ time with $\delta_{\rm bad}=\min\{1,80(f-1)2^{-K}\}$, which is $O(V(L^\tau+1))$ for the layer's parameters.
children.method: Realize the XOR by eight parity-controlled $\pm1$ updates applied to all $K$-bit segments at once as single cyclic shifts of whole chunks, then repair deterministically the few addresses whose guard values let a segment carry into the next.

motivation.text: A chunk-wide cyclic shift updates all $f$ segments in one linear pass; carries between segments can occur only at a fraction $O(f2^{-K})$ of addresses, small enough to fix by sorting just those records.

quote.quote:
Also $K/\log p\to\infty$, which will
make the exceptional set in a packed change of address bits small enough
to repair by sorting.

children.claim: With a Boolean control $c$, the eight updates induce the cycle $(00\ 01\ 10)$ and then $(01\ 10\ 11)$ on the parities of $(u,w)$, so the result is $(u+c(1-2(u\bmod2)),w)$: the parity of $u$ flips exactly when $c=1$, both quotients by two are kept, the auxiliary $w$ is restored, and no coordinate ever moves by more than four.

quote.quote:
Thus the parity of $u$
is flipped precisely when $c=1$, both quotients under division by two are
preserved, and the arbitrary auxiliary integer $w$ is restored.

children.claim: Applied to all segments $[j_i,j_i+K)$, $i<f-1$, at once, each update is the single cyclic shift $y\gets y+\varepsilon\sum_i2^{j_i}[x_{j_i}=1][z_{j_i}=b]\pmod{2^L}$ (or the same with $y,z$ exchanged), whose offset never depends on its target, so it is a bijection done by chunk swaps and one controlled shift.

quote.quote:
The shift offset never depends on its target chunk, so each line is a
bijection of the rectangle.

children.claim: Outside the set $\mathcal B$ of addresses where some guard value $g$ fails $10\le g\le2^{K-1}-11$, no segment carries into or borrows from the next, so the composed shifts $S_0$ agree with the ideal map $T_0$; the addresses in $\mathcal B$ are the only exceptions.

quote.quote:
no segment carries into or borrows
from the next segment.

children.claim: Each guard excludes twenty of its $2^{K-1}$ values and the full $y,z$ ranges give every spectator the same guard distribution, so the union bound over $2(f-1)$ guards gives $|\mathcal B|\le\delta_{\rm bad}M$ independently of the records.

quote.quote:
Indeed, the complete $y,z$ ranges give the same guard distribution at
each choice of spectator coordinates.

children.claim: Both $S_0$ and $T_0$ are bijections that agree off $\mathcal B$, and $T_0$ preserves $\mathcal B$, so the correction $T_0S_0^{-1}$ only permutes $\mathcal B$; its records are extracted with destination ranks, radix-sorted and reinserted.

quote.quote: Thus $T_0S_0^{-1}$ fixes $\mathcal B^c$ and permutes $\mathcal B$.

children.claim: The omitted top position $j_{f-1}$ is done by one two-bit XOR in $O(V)$; when $f=1$ this is the whole procedure.

quote.quote: This costs $O(V)$ and supplies the omitted selected position.

children.claim: After division by $V$ the extra terms are $A_{\rm rect}^3/R\to0$ and $O(p^22^{-K}(1+A_{\rm rect}/R))=o(1)$ when $R$ exceeds every polynomial in $p$ and $K/\log p\to\infty$.

quote.quote:
Under the stated family bounds
the first tends to zero, and the second is
$O(p^2 2^{-K}(1+A_{\rm rect}/R))=o(1)$.

children.salient: The time bound is worst-case and deterministic although the cheap shifts are wrong on some addresses: the exceptional set depends only on addresses, never on the data.

children.claim: A fixed binary change of basis on $e=mf$ axes is a fixed number of row additions, each one packed selected-bit addition with two slots as $x,y$ and a third slot as $z$, so it and its inverse cost $O(V((eK)^\tau+1))$.

quote.quote:
the complete change of basis and its inverse therefore cost
$O(V((eK)^\tau+1))$ on a stream of volume $V$.
